source_text: Ex hoc intellegi debere perfectam ignorantiam iustitiam nominari, quia dixit Deus ad Abimelech, qui cum Sarra fuerat concubiturus, ignorans quod uxor esset aliena: Et ego sciebam quia in corde mundo fecisti hoc . Et ideo nascentium statum, generantium voluntate non laedi: quia etsi mala esset tamen ad illorum nullo genere scientiam perveniret Nec iustos nasci parvulos, nec iniustos, quod futuri sunt actibus suis; sed tantummodo infantiam innocentiae dote locupletem? Homo igitur innocentia quidem plenus, sed virtutis capax nascitur, aut laudem, aut reprehensionem ex proposito accedente, meriturus
pass_a_gloss: From this to-be-understood to-owe perfectam ignorantiam justice nominari, because he-said God to Abimelech, who when/with Sarah fuerat concubiturus, ignorans that/which uxor would-be others'-things: and ego sciebam because in in-the-heart in-the-world fecisti this. and for-that-reason nascentium statum, generantium by-will not laedi: because even-if evils would-be nevertheless to illorum by-no genere scientiam perveniret nor iustos to-be-born parvulos, nor iniustos, that/which futuri are actibus his-own; but tantummodo infancy innocentiae dote locupletem? human-being therefore innocentia indeed full, but of-virtue capable is-born, or laudem, or reprehensionem from proposito accedente, meriturus.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: Complete ignorance should be understood to be called righteousness, because God said to Abimelech, who was about to lie with Sarah without knowing that she was another man’s wife: “I too knew that you did this with a clean heart” (Genesis 20:6). Thus the condition of those who are born is not harmed by the will of those who conceive them. Even if that will were evil, it would not come within the children’s knowledge in any way.
Infants are born neither righteous nor unrighteous; their own actions will make them so. Infancy is simply rich with the gift of innocence.
A human being is therefore born full of innocence, but capable of virtue, and will deserve praise or blame according to the purpose subsequently chosen.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Glossary: avoid modern merit-theology; Julian means deserved outcome.
